experience.title: Grating Metasurface Based Broadband Absorber for Thermal Emitter
experience.description: Modelled a 1D grating structure which synergistically utilized plasmonic, cavity and magnetic modes, offering a broadband absorber with 2584 nm bandwith and 95.90% average absorption. We showed the structure can be good candidate for thermal emitter.

experience.title: Metasurface Based Color Router Using PSO
experience.description: Designed a Metasurface that mimics the Bayer's color filter. We utilized this color router along with Perovskite-based photo-detector to implement a image sensor. [ Manuscript is under preparation]

experience.title: Fano-Resonant All-Dielectric Metasurface Governed by Q-BIC
experience.description: Designed a bow-tie nanohole-patterned cuboid metasurface supporting multiple quasi-BIC–induced Fano resonances. Achieved high-Q modes (10³–10⁴) with near-unity modulation depth and strong spectral contrast. Performed FDTD simulations, theoretical fitting, and multipolar decomposition to elucidate resonance origins and validate BIC behavior. Demonstrated polarization-dependent response and high refractive index sensitivity (342 nm/RIU, FOM ≈ 217), showing potential for active optical switching and biosensing applications.

experience.title: Hybrid Metal-Dielectric Nanostructure Integrated Solar Cell
experience.description: We designed and analyzed a c-Si/TiO₂ heterojunction thin-film solar cell incorporating Ag–AZO hybrid metal–dielectric nanostructures (HMDN) to mitigate ohmic losses and enhance light absorption. Using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations, we showed that the triangular HMDN pair significantly improved long-wavelength absorption through strong field confinement and directional scattering, while TiO₂, ITO, and SiO₂ pyramid layers enhanced short-wavelength absorption by extending the optical path.The optimized structure achieved an average absorption of 83.32%, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 37.96 mA/cm², and a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 17.42%, with only 0.34% variation under polarization change. The inclusion of HMDN resulted in a 4.54% efficiency enhancement compared to conventional designs, demonstrating their effectiveness in improving the performance of thin-film solar cells.

experience.title: Metasurface-based Color Filter
experience.description: We designed and analyzed a Si–SiO₂–Si dielectric metasurface to achieve polarization-dependent structural colorization by exploiting refractive index contrast. Using FDTD simulations, we studied optical responses and electric field distributions, revealing strong light–matter interactions and asymmetric reflection behavior. Through parametric optimization, we achieved a high color difference (~68) for TE-polarized light with minimal loss and maintained stable performance (~20) up to a 60° incident angle. Our work demonstrates the potential of dielectric metasurfaces for hyperspectral imaging, color filtering, and anti-counterfeiting applications.

experience.title: Plasmon-Enhanced c-Si Thin-Film Solar Cell
experience.description: We designed an n–p junction c-Si thin-film solar cell featuring Ag nanostructured back reflectors and inverted triangular grooves for enhanced light trapping. Using FDTD simulations, we achieved 84.36% average absorption, Jsc of 40.66 mA/cm², and efficiency of 17.25%. The structure maintained strong performance across 0°–60° incidence angles, and optimization of the unit cell period further improved efficiency, demonstrating the potential of plasmonic nanostructures for high-efficiency solar cells.

experience.title: GaP-Based Photonic Crystals for Band Gap Engineering
experience.description: We investigated gallium phosphide (GaP) photonic crystals with various lattice geometries—triangular, hexagonal, and honeycomb—for both hole and rod configurations to study their band gap characteristics. By performing a comparative band structure analysis, we identified a wide photonic band gap (103.77–340.91 THz) and examined the magnetic field distribution to explain the underlying gap formation mechanism. Our results include a comprehensive gap-map for GaP-based PCs, providing design guidelines for achieving desired frequency responses. This study demonstrates the potential of GaP photonic crystals for fiber-optic and far-infrared photonic applications.
